item.title: Mise
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
Mise
https://mise.jdx.dev/
Your dev env,already prepped. One tool to manage languages, env vars, and tasks per project, reproducibly.

Everything in its place, before you code.
In a professional kitchen, mise en place is the ritual of prep: knives sharpened, onions diced, stock warm, station clean. The work before the work.
mise does the same for your dev env. It activates the right language versions, loads the right env vars, and wires up the right tasks for the commands you run.

item.title: xc
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
xc - Simple, Convenient, Docs-based task runner.
https://xcfile.dev/

xc is a task runner similar to Make or npm run, that aims to be more discoverable and approachable.

The problem xc is intended to solve is scripts maintained separately from their documentation. Often a Makefile or a package.json will contain some useful scripts for developing on a project, then the README.md will surface and describe these scripts. In such a case, since the documentation is separate, it may not be updated when scripts are changed or added. xc aims to solve this by defining the scripts inline with the documentation.

item.title: Apache Shenyu
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
Apache Shenyu
Java native API Gateway for service proxy, protocol conversion and API governance.
https://shenyu.apache.org/

https://github.com/apache/shenyu

Feature List

- Language: provides .NET, Python, Go, Java client for API register
- Proxy: Support for Apache® Dubbo™, Spring Cloud, gRPC, Motan, SOFA, TARS, WebSocket, MQTT
- Security: Sign, OAuth 2.0, JSON Web Tokens, WAF plugin
- API governance: Request, response, parameter mapping, Hystrix, RateLimiter plugin
- Observability: Tracing, metrics, logging plugin
- Extensions: Plugin hot-swapping, dynamic loading
- Dashboard: Dynamic traffic control, visual backend for user menu permissions
- Cluster: NGINX, Docker, Kubernetes

item.title: Hey
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
Hey
https://github.com/rakyll/hey

hey is a tiny program that sends some load to a web application.

hey was originally called boom and was influenced from Tarek Ziade’s tool at tarekziade/boom.

Using the same name was a mistake as it resulted in cases where binary name conflicts created confusion.
To preserve the name for its original owner, we renamed this project to hey.

Previously known as github.com/rakyll/boom.
